note: Sources for the page site/src/seeding.html. Every statement about how IllustrisTNG and SIMBA seed black holes is a sentence from one of the papers below (field 'text'; field 'latex' is the same sentence as it stands in the TeX source of the arXiv version, with only the markup of mathematics and citations changed in 'text'), or a sentence of a file in this repository (checked word for word by scripts/test-site.mjs). The papers were read on the date given; the SHA-256 is that of the arXiv source archive that was read. Nothing else about seeding is stated on the page. Not reviewed by anyone outside the project.

camels.cite: Villaescusa-Navarro et al. 2021, ApJ 915, 71 (the CAMELS paper)
camels.why: It is the source named for the catalogues in data/ensembles/camels-galaxies.json, so it describes the two models as they were run in the experiment this study uses.

weinberger.cite: Weinberger et al. 2017 (the black hole model of IllustrisTNG)
weinberger.why: It is listed as a paper of IllustrisTNG in data/simulation-profiles.json.

dave.cite: Davé et al. 2019, MNRAS 486, 2827 (the SIMBA paper)
dave.why: It is listed as the overview paper of SIMBA in data/simulation-profiles.json.

quotes.where: Section "Simulations", introduction (the cosmological parameters that are fixed in all simulations)

quotes.text: SMBH particles with initial mass M_seed = 8×10⁵ M☉ h⁻¹ are seeded in halos with mass M_FoF > 5×10¹⁰ M☉ h⁻¹.
quotes.latex: SMBH particles with initial mass $M_{\rm seed} = 8\times10^5$\,\Msunh~are seeded in halos with mass $M_{\rm FoF}> 5\times10^{10}$\,\Msunh.

quotes.where: Section "Accretion estimate and seeding of black holes"
quotes.text: In our cosmological simulations, a black hole with mass M_seed is placed at the centre of a halo whenever the on-the-fly friend-of-friends halo finder identifies a halo more massive than a threshold mass M_FOF that does not yet contain a black hole.
quotes.latex: In our cosmological simulations, a black hole with mass $M_\text{seed}$ is placed at the centre of a halo whenever the on-the-fly friend-of-friends halo finder identifies a halo more massive than a threshold mass $M_\text{FOF}$ that does not yet contain a black hole.

quotes.where: Section "Accretion estimate and seeding of black holes"
quotes.text: Given the significant theoretical uncertainties in the early growth of SMBHs [citation omitted], we consider the seed mass as a poorly constrained free parameter.
quotes.latex: Given the significant theoretical uncertainties in the early growth of SMBHs \citep[e.g.][]{2010A&ARv..18..279V}, we consider the seed mass as a poorly constrained free parameter.

quotes.text: Black holes with initial mass M_seed = 10⁴ M☉ h⁻¹ are seeded in galaxies with M⋆ ≳ 10^9.5 M☉ by means of the on-the-fly FoF, with the M⋆ threshold for seeding motivated by FIRE simulations showing that stellar feedback strongly suppresses black hole growth in lower mass galaxies [citations omitted].
quotes.latex: Black holes with initial mass $M_{\rm seed} = 10^4$\,\Msunh~are seeded in galaxies with $M_{\star} \gtrsim 10^{9.5}$\,\Msun~by means of the on-the-fly FoF, with the $M_{\star}$ threshold for seeding motivated by FIRE simulations showing that stellar feedback strongly suppresses black hole growth in lower mass galaxies

quotes.text: If a galaxy reaches a stellar mass M⋆ > γ_BH × M_seed and it does not already contain a black hole particle, then the star particle closest to the center of mass of the galaxy is converted into a black hole particle. For our fiducial simulations, we employ M_seed = 10⁴ M☉/h and γ_BH = 3×10⁵, which places black holes in galaxies with M⋆ ≳ 10^9.5 M☉.
quotes.latex: If a galaxy reaches a stellar mass $M_{*} > \gamma_{\rm BH} \times M_{\rm seed}$ and it does not already contain a black hole particle, then the star particle closest to the center of mass of the galaxy is converted into a black hole particle.  For our fiducial simulations, we employ $M_{\rm seed} = 10^4$\,M$_{\odot}/h$~and $\gamma_{\rm BH} = 3\times10^5$, which places black holes in galaxies with $M_{*} \gtrsim 10^{9.5}$\,M$_{\odot}$.

quotes.where: Section "Cosmological and astrophysical properties", paragraph "Galaxy black hole masses"
quotes.text: We find good agreement between the median black hole masses of both simulation suites; however those for the SIMBA set drop quickly for stellar masses below ~5×10⁹ h⁻¹ M☉, owing to the black hole seeding model [citations omitted]; this feature is not observed in the IllustrisTNG set.
quotes.latex: We find good agreement between the median black hole masses of both simulation suites; however those for the SIMBA set drop quickly for stellar masses below $\sim5\times10^9~h^{-1}M_\odot$, owing to the black hole seeding model \citep{SIMBA,Thomas2019}; this feature is not observed in the IllustrisTNG set.

quotes.text: In the hydrodynamic simulations, besides Ω_m, σ_8, and the initial random seed, we also vary the value of four astrophysical parameters related to stellar and AGN feedback. [...] While we do not consider parameter variations for other key baryonic processes, we explore variations over a broad range of efficiencies for some of the most important and uncertain feedback processes in galaxy formation: galactic winds driven by supernovae (SNe) and kinetic feedback from massive black holes.
quotes.latex: In the hydrodynamic simulations, besides $\Omega_{\rm m}$, $\sigma_8$, and the initial random seed, we also vary the value of four astrophysical parameters related to stellar and AGN feedback.|While we do not consider parameter variations for other key baryonic processes, we explore variations over a broad range of efficiencies for some of the most important and uncertain feedback processes in galaxy formation: galactic winds driven by supernovae (SNe) and kinetic feedback from massive black holes.
